title: On Calling the children in from the field
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：call　|　正文 357 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 call 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 the gardener ① called the children in from the field year after year, and every apprentice in the garden said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three springs on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the gardener ② calls the children in from the field for the whole place without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ call the children in from the field at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ called the children in from the field before — a line in the notebook for April 1942 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Calling the children in from the field year after year, the gardener said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the trowel at the far bed, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ call the doctor in town for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Call the doctor in town at once and never mention it again.

By 1955 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the notebook, and a new apprentice from the next garden ⑧ calls the doctor in town year after year every spring without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the bed, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ called the children in from the field again when nobody else would.

⑩ To call the children in from the field, my mother said in 1960, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the garden remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the garden forgets, somebody calls the children in from the field for the whole place again and somebody must call the children in from the field year after year all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 唤回（一般过去式 called the children in from the field：1948 年园丁头一回这样做，年年地）
B. v. 唤回（一般现在 calls the children in from the field：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 唤回（不定式 to call the children in from the field：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 唤回（过去完成时 had called the children in from the field：1942 年四月的园艺笔记上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 唤回（动名词 calling the children in from the field 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 打电话给（call the doctor in town：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去打电话给城里的那位医生）
G. v. 打电话给（call the doctor in town：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 唤回（后段两处：新来的学徒照例 calls the doctor in town，而母亲又一次 called the children in from the field）

call 意为“唤回”，自那以后园丁替所有人把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 calls。
call 意为“唤回”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯唤回把孩子们从地里唤回来”，此处为不定式 to call the children in from the field。
call 意为“唤回”，园艺笔记里 四月 那行字说明早在 1955 年之前就有人唤回过，故用过去完成时 had called。
call 意为“唤回”，园丁说“唤回把孩子们从地里唤回来这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 calling the children in from the field 作主语。
call 意为“打电话给”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去打电话给城里的那位医生”，should ever 之后用原形 call the doctor in town。
call 意为“打电话给”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻打电话给城里的那位医生（call the doctor in town at once），以后再也不要提起。
call 意为“唤回”，新来的学徒每个春天都照例打电话给城里的那位医生，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 calls。
call 意为“唤回”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次年年地唤回把孩子们从地里唤回来，用一般过去式 called 叙述。
call 意为“唤回”，结尾那句是母亲 1960 年的话：要唤回把孩子们从地里唤回来，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和园子记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 call 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1948 the gardener called the children in from the field year after year, and nobody in the garden forgot it.
Even now the gardener calls the children in from the field for the whole place whenever the garden asks.
Calling the children in from the field year after year, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever call the doctor in town for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new apprentice from the next garden calls the doctor in town year after year every spring, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother called the children in from the field again, and the garden remembered that half.
